problem_text:
A logistics manager needs to select packages for a cargo shipment. The available packages are:
* Package 1: size 41 cubic feet, revenue $157
* Package 2: size 44 cubic feet, revenue $258
* Package 3: size 10 cubic feet, revenue $214
* Package 4: size 44 cubic feet, revenue $230
* Package 5: size 26 cubic feet, revenue $164
* Package 6: size 31 cubic feet, revenue $290
* Package 7: size 24 cubic feet, revenue $165
* Package 8: size 27 cubic feet, revenue $97
* Package 9: size 23 cubic feet, revenue $29
* Package 10: size 28 cubic feet, revenue $234
* Package 11: size 29 cubic feet, revenue $168
* Package 12: size 5 cubic feet, revenue $126
* Package 13: size 22 cubic feet, revenue $128
* Package 14: size 25 cubic feet, revenue $22
* Package 15: size 40 cubic feet, revenue $183
* Package 16: size 10 cubic feet, revenue $103
* Package 17: size 32 cubic feet, revenue $45
* Package 18: size 50 cubic feet, revenue $60
* Package 19: size 12 cubic feet, revenue $26
* Package 20: size 15 cubic feet, revenue $101

The cargo container has a maximum capacity of 376 cubic feet. Choose the package combination that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this capacity limit. Each package must be either fully accepted or rejected.
